title: Three hundred (Judges 7)
hookLine: the army is cut to three hundred so no one thinks numbers won

cards: Thirty-two thousand men camp by the spring of Harod, with Midian spread out in the valley below. For a man who asked for sign after sign, it should be a comfort.
Then the Lord speaks to Gideon, and it's the last thing a nervous general wants to hear. Not: you need more. The opposite.
The people that are with thee are too many.

teach.h: TOO MANY, OR THEY'LL CREDIT THEMSELVES.
teach.b: The reason is given straight out: "lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me." If a big army wins, everyone credits the big army. So the cutting starts.
Whoever is fearful and trembling may go home. Twenty-two thousand leave; ten thousand stay. Still too many.
Gideon brings them down to the water, and the Lord sorts them by how they drink.
Three hundred bring the water up in their hands and lap it. The rest kneel down to drink, and go home. The text never says why lapping was the test; the point seems to be the cut, not the method.
Then a tender detail. That night God tells Gideon to attack, and adds: if you're afraid, take your servant Purah and go listen at the edge of the camp first. Even now, the fear is planned for.
Gideon overhears a soldier telling a dream: a loaf of barley bread tumbles into the camp and flattens a tent. The battle itself is strange.

teach.h: JARS, TORCHES, SHOFARS: STAND IN PLACE.
teach.b: The three hundred carry shofars, and torches hidden inside empty jars. They surround the camp, smash the jars, blow, and shout: "The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon."
Then they stand, each man in his place, and the camp panics and flees. In the story, three hundred were enough, because the numbers were never what won.

how: Jews read Gideon's three hundred as part of studying Judges, and teachers often point to the stated reason for the cut: so that Israel would not say its own hand had saved it.

games.q: you're Gideon, with thirty-two thousand men and an enemy filling the valley. God says: too many. what do you do?
o: send messengers for more men, just in case.
let the afraid go home, then cut again at the water.
keep everyone, but hold most of them back.
games.why: twenty-two thousand go home, then only the three hundred who lapped stay, so that no one can say, mine own hand hath saved me.

practice: Rest your hands open and empty in your lap, and breathe. Picture one ordinary task done with less than you think you need, fewer words, one dish instead of three, and notice that it's enough.
If you pray, let the shout of the three hundred remind you who gets the credit.
